item.title: Kotohiragu Autumn Festival — Guide
item.description: The Kotohiragu Autumn Festival is the great annual celebration of Konpira-san, the beloved shrine above Kotohira, held over several days in October. Its highlight is a solemn and stately procession in which a portable shrine (mikoshi) carrying the deity is borne down the shrine’s famous long stone stairway and through the town, accompanied by priests, attendants in traditional costume, and ceremonial regalia — a dignified spectacle rooted in centuries of tradition.

item.title: Kotohiragu Shrine: The 785-Step Climb — Guide
item.description: Kotohiragu, affectionately known as Konpira-san, is one of Japan’s most beloved shrines, dedicated to the guardian deity of seafarers and long a pilgrimage destination drawing visitors from across the country. It sits high on the wooded slopes of Mount Zozu above the town of Kotohira, and reaching it is famously a climb: a stone stairway of 785 steps to the main shrine, or 1,368 all the way to the inner shrine.
